methodological_rigor.justification: This prospective longitudinal study enrolled 50 postoperative breast cancer patients via convenience sampling and measured QoL (FACT-B), functional exercise compliance, fear of cancer recurrence (FCRI-SF), and sleep quality (PSQI) at three time points (pre-discharge, 1 month, 3 months), with 4 participants lost to follow-up (7.4%). The measurement instruments and data collection procedures are described in detail, but the single-center convenience sample and modest size limit generalizability and the stability of multivariable/path estimates. The analysis uses repeated-measures comparisons, generalized estimating equations (with an unstructured correlation matrix and VIF checks), and structural equation modeling with bootstrap resampling; these methods fit the longitudinal/correlational question, but causal inference remains limited and the manuscript itself flags potential overfitting (e.g., RMSEA reported as 0.000).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The outcomes (postoperative QoL, sleep, fear of recurrence, and exercise adherence) are clinically relevant for survivorship care and rehabilitation planning after breast cancer surgery. The cohort reports substantial QoL changes over time (FACT-B mean 87.44 at T1 rising to 104.16 at T2 and 100.50 at T3) and finds associations where fear of recurrence and poorer sleep are negatively related to QoL, with exercise compliance showing a marginally positive direct effect in path analysis (p=0.052). As a single prospective observational cohort without intervention randomization, the Oxford LoE is best classified as 2b.

reporting_quality.justification: This is an observational cohort study, so STROBE is the closest checklist; the manuscript reports eligibility criteria, recruitment setting, measurement tools (including reliability details), time points, handling of attrition (GEE under MCAR), and the main analytic approaches (GEE and SEM with bootstrap). Limitations are explicitly discussed (small single-center sample, convenience sampling/selection bias, self-report bias, and caution about perfect fit indices). Data/code availability is not stated in the blinded text (no dataset or analysis code repository mentioned), supporting only limited reproducibility from description.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is moderate: the manuscript integrates functional exercise adherence, fear of recurrence, and sleep quality in a three-timepoint longitudinal framework and uses path analysis to articulate direct and indirect associations. The constructs and instruments are well established, and the sample is small, so the contribution is more in the specific modeled relationships and temporal framing than in a new concept or intervention. The manuscript appropriately positions findings as exploratory and calls for larger validation.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract reports key design features, sample, instruments, and main coefficients (including beta estimates and confidence intervals for GEE predictors), which supports interpretability. Methods are detailed for survey tools and statistical analyses (including fit indices and bootstrap approach), and results are organized across timepoint comparisons, GEE predictors, and the path model. Some presentation quirks remain (e.g., methods content appearing later in the document structure), but overall clarity and specificity are good.

key_strengths: Prospective three-timepoint follow-up with validated instruments (FACT-B, FCRI-SF, PSQI) and explicit reporting of QoL trajectories over 3 months.
Use of longitudinal modeling (GEE) and mediation-style path analysis with bootstrap resampling to explore direct and indirect associations.
Limitations are acknowledged clearly, including sample size, convenience sampling, and the risk of overfitting suggested by perfect fit indices.
key_concerns: Small single-center convenience sample (n=50) limits power and stability of the SEM/path model and increases risk of overfitting (RMSEA reported as 0.000).
Causal language should be carefully constrained; associations may reflect unmeasured confounding despite longitudinal measurement.
No stated data/code sharing in the blinded manuscript, limiting reproducibility and external scrutiny.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a well-written exploratory observational cohort analysis with clinically relevant survivorship endpoints, but the small convenience sample and potential model overfitting mean it is most plausible in a mid-tier clinical nursing/rehabilitation outlet after major revisions and stronger robustness checks.
